clue.text: Place never represented in measure of popularity?

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in another form, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a place nobody has ever portrayed, in a popularity survey.
explanation.definitionFit: How widespread something is, its prevalence, is a gauge of how popular or common it has become.

clue.text: Scheduled League clash?

parts.note: something scheduled is due at a set time

explanation.surface: A fixture in the football league between two rival sides, set for a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a fight between two parties, a head-to-head clash or contest.

clue.text: Move at chess? Players initially look edgy

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the two words that follow it

explanation.surface: A chess game where the competitors are visibly on edge as they ponder their first move.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess move in which king and rook shift together, so to make that move is this verb.

clue.text: Explanatory material little encountered in essential stuff given to Academy

indicators.note: something encountered in a place is found within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the meat of something is its essential substance
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A description of supplementary notes, briefly glimpsed among core content submitted to an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' reads as an adjective on 'encountered', but it is a noun, a tad; 'encountered in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metadata is data describing other data, material that explains what a dataset contains.

clue.text: A timeless story supported by song and dance connoisseur

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above is held up by the one beneath, so this one follows
being without time means the abbreviation T for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: a story is a work of fiction
a song and dance is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: A story without a date, borne along by musical numbers, as if describing a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T from FICTION to leave FICION.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen and knowledgeable enthusiast, an expert devotee of some pursuit.

clue.text: Malevolent spirit turning up in fireplace

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read in the opposite direction
in tells us the letters lie inside the word fireplace

explanation.surface: A wicked ghost rising up the chimney from the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks IREP from fIREPlace, and 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth this fairy being was originally thought of as an evil sprite before becoming benign.

clue.text: Woman about to enter English resort, spurning European

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it
spurning means rejecting, so the letter is removed

parts.note: MARGATE is a seaside resort in Kent, on England's south-east coast
re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A woman heading for an English seaside town but turning down a foreigner from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurning' drops E from MARGATE to leave MARGAT, which RE enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Top show almost missing its slot for broadcast

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a circus is performed under the big top
something that has missed its appointed time slot is late

explanation.surface: A top-rated programme nearly failing to get its scheduled airtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like 'best', but it is the big top of a circus.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to spread it around widely, to put it into circulation.

clue.text: Swear nothing is omitted from part of meal

indicators.note: a thing omitted from a word is taken out of it

parts.note: a meal is served in stages, each a course
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone cursing because nothing has been left out of a dinner course.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to use profanity, to utter an oath or a bad word.

clue.text: Nothing about revolutionary woman

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, slang for nothing at all
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that there is nothing to say about some radical woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Contestant's appearance ignoring a rule

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: putting in an appearance is coming on the scene, an arrival

explanation.surface: A competitor's turning up while disregarding one of the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a contest faces an opponent; each is a contender against the other.

clue.text: Material on roof: that feature's beginning to grate

parts.note: the chin is one of the features of the face

indicators.note: beginning tells us to take just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A complaint that the straw on a roof is starting to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means a facial feature, not a characteristic of the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid on a roof as a covering is the traditional cottage roofing material.

clue.text: Bits of film presented in middle of week showing astronomical phenomenon

indicators.note: something presented in another is placed inside it
the middle of a word is its letters without the two ends

parts.note: short extracts of film are clips

explanation.surface: A midweek screening of footage of a celestial event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of week' means the inner letters of the word, not Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon blocks the sun, or the earth shadows the moon, the sky shows this event.

clue.text: Holy times reanimated after priest offers Hindu belief?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the priest's letter
reanimated means brought back to life in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sacred festivals revived under a cleric's lead in an Indian religious practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Hinduism as just one example of belief in many gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinduism honours many deities, an example of worshipping more than one god.

clue.text: Someone who tries things is tense when cornered by a drug user

indicators.note: something cornered by others is hemmed in, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: a doper is someone who takes drugs
T is a standard grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An experimenter getting nervous when trapped by a junkie.
explanation.walkthrough: The T sits within A plus DOPER, between the P and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes up new products or ideas, as in an early adopter, is willing to try them.

clue.text: Traffic merging, say — it requires a lot of workers

definitions.text: it requires a lot of workers

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, especially illicitly
a merging is an example of a union, two joined as one

explanation.surface: Road traffic converging, observed as a job needing many hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour body for collective bargaining depends on having many members from the workforce.

clue.text: No sarky comments about bridge team offering some security

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: lip is cheek, sarcastic back-talk
North and South form a partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A bridge pair avoiding snide remarks to stay safe.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface with grip that stops feet sliding gives a degree of safety.

clue.text: Unexpectedly tamed one parasitic worm

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Surprise at one tamed parasite worming its way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundworm, many species of which live as parasites in animals and plants.

clue.text: Prince taking on monster to get further

parts.note: an ogress is a female monster

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale prince fighting a monster to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' just joins the two pieces in a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance or move forward is to make headway, going further.

clue.text: Absolutely certain woman is to reject first soldier

indicators.note: rejecting the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a madam is a lady, a woman
a soldier ant is a worker of a certain caste

explanation.surface: A woman, sure of herself, turning away the leading soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first soldier' looks like one phrase; 'first' goes with 'reject' and the soldier is an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely sure and unbending in an opinion is unyielding.

clue.text: Conductor confused situation, overlooking line and metre

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so these letters are left out

parts.note: a maelstrom is a whirl of turmoil
M is the symbol for metre

explanation.surface: A conductor in a muddle, missing a line of music and its metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A great orchestral leader or other master musician is given this title.

clue.text: Farmers gutted about cow plants

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it
a gutted word loses its insides, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate, which is one sense of lower, to frown or look sullen and threatening

explanation.surface: Devastated farmers fussing over a cow and their crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is a verb here, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooms are plants grown for their blossoms.

clue.text: Soccer group's discretion upset rich businessman?

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, England's football governing body

indicators.note: in a down clue being upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: discretion is tact

explanation.surface: The football authorities' tactful silence being overturned over a wealthy tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for a wealthy, powerful executive; the question mark notes it need not be a businessman.

clue.text: Speak about Democrat and Liberal with regret

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: to speak is to say

explanation.surface: A politician talking ruefully about two rival parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something regretfully is to do it sorrowfully, unhappily.

clue.text: Not for many to know with respect to changing

indicators.note: changing means the letters are altered in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: An official phrase about something altering, as if from a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with respect to' looks like a single phrase, but 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified material is restricted to very few people with clearance.

clue.text: Look — alloy has no little weight

indicators.note: having no part means it is taken away

parts.note: pewter is a tin-based alloy
wt is the short form, the little version, of weight

explanation.surface: Telling us to look at some metal that weighs hardly anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely, squinting at something.

clue.text: Return of academics keeping year for religious meeting

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
a return sends the word back the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: dons are university lecturers

explanation.surface: University teachers coming back for a year to a church council.
explanation.definitionFit: A council of clergy, and often laity, assembled to decide church matters.

clue.text: 15's upset about hospital offering no openings

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it
in a down clue being upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the answer to 15 down is abbreviated TU, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Workers' organisation angered about the hospital having no vacancies.
explanation.walkthrough: TUS reversed gives SUT, which goes about H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something closed has no gaps or way in.

clue.text: Doctor, say, drawn to singular contents of used bottle?

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
S is a standard grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A doctor attracted to an odd bottle's remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The sediment left in the bottom of a finished bottle is the residue.

clue.text: Legally required to stop imprisoning teacher

indicators.note: imprisoning something means holding it inside

parts.note: to stay is to stop, as in stay of execution
a tutor is a teacher

explanation.surface: A legal requirement to halt the jailing of a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposed by statute, by a law, so mandatory.
